area: Foundation models for cell segmentation (zero-shot / few-shot / fine-tune) for PC12 phase-contrast + fluorescence morphometrics

candidates.name: Cellpose-SAM (v4.x, cpsam/cpsam_v2) + CellposeDINO (cpdino)
candidates.what_it_does: Generalist 2D/3D cell & nucleus instance segmentation. Flow-field (star-convex vector) decoder on top of a SAM-ViT-L or DINOv3-ViT-L/B backbone; robust to shot noise, blur, anisotropy, channel shuffling, cell size; trained on 22,826 images / 3.34M cells (light microscopy + histopathology). Official human-in-the-loop fine-tuning in GUI/notebook; exports to BioImage.IO. Built-in models: cpsam_v2 (Jun 2026, low-contrast fix), cpsam (Apr 2025), cpdino, cpdino-vitb.
candidates.pc12_fit: Excellent for cell BODIES in phase contrast: the MIDL 2026 benchmark (Archit & Pape, arXiv:2603.17845) found CellPose-SAM consistently in the top-3 on label-free (phase-contrast-type) microscopy datasets; the Cellpose paper itself reports phase-contrast (LIVEcell, HeLa) as a core training domain. Neurites: NO — it is a single-class star-convex instance model; its pretrained models target cyto/nuclei/both. Thin tubular neurites violate the star-convex-from-soma assumption (long 2-3 px arms will be dropped, truncated, or swallowed into the body mask), so it CANNOT represent the neurite class natively. You could fine-tune a custom class, but star-convex geometry is a poor shape prior for branching dendrites — expect clDice-style failure. Verdict: use it as the cell-body engine, not the neurite engine.
candidates.neurite_support: No native neurite class; star-convex shape prior actively hostile to long thin branches (reasoned estimate from geometry; no PC12-neurite evaluation found in the paper)
candidates.license: Code: BSD-3-Clause (permissive, fine for student + commercial-free use). CAVEAT from official README: ALL pretrained models and the annotated Cellpose dataset are CC-BY-NC (non-commercial) — fine for a thesis, not for a product. The README badge says 'GPL v3' but the LICENSE file is BSD-3-Clause (verified both; GitHub API reports bsd-3-clause).
candidates.compute: Inference: tiny on RTX A5000 (seconds/image, ViT-L ~300M params, fits in <10 GB VRAM with margin to spare). Fine-tuning: hours overnight on A5000 (small CNN-flow decoder head trained on your 70 images + ROIs; the documented workflow assumes dozens of images, not thousands — the BIBM 2025 data-efficiency study (arXiv:2511.04803) confirms Cellpose fine-tunes effectively on small labeled sets).
candidates.small_data_fit: Best-in-class: Cellpose 2.0 was explicitly designed for human-in-the-loop training on tens of images; n=70 labeled images + second batch is exactly the intended regime.
candidates.effort: Low (pip install, GUI or 10-line API; train_Cellpose-SAM.ipynb provided)
candidates.notes: W6-gate zero-shot run: use cpsam_v2 (or cpdino) with a calibrated diameter; expect good cell-body instance masks on phase contrast, expect neurite loss. Fine-tune track: 2-5 h GPU + a few hundred clicks of ROI corrections; produces your own per-class models you own (train on your own labels — your labels aren't subject to CC-BY-NC). Instance masks: YES (labelmap) — best candidate for touching-cell counting.

candidates.name: StarDist 2D/3D (v1, plus 2025 single-shot extension)
candidates.what_it_does: CNN predicts per-pixel polygon radii along N rays + probability; NMS yields instances. Pretrained 2D_versatile_fluo (DSB2018 nuclei) and 2D_versatile_he. Multi-class instance+classification supported; built-in stardist.matching for PQ/precision/recall. 2025 paper (arXiv:2504.12078) shows single-shot star-convex variants beating Cellpose baseline on spatially-correlated objects.
candidates.pc12_fit: Weaker than Cellpose zero-shot on phase contrast: pretrained models are FLUORESCENCE-nuclei / H&E only — no phase-contrast pretrained weight; zero-shot on PC12 brightfield/phase will underperform Cellpose (inference estimate; the MIDL 2026 survey lists StarDist among models that degrade on out-of-domain label-free data). BUT StarDist is the easiest to fine-tune from scratch on n=70: small U-Net-like model, ~1 h on A5000, TF or PyTorch. Same star-convex limitation: cell bodies fine, neurites no. 2D_versatile_fluo CAN be applied to your fluorescence channel if you have a body/stain channel and it happens to look like DSB2018-ish objects.
candidates.neurite_support: No (star-convex shape prior; cannot represent long thin branches)
candidates.compute: Inference: seconds/image on A5000. Fine-tune: ~1-2 h on A5000 for n≈50 images (well-trodden; notebook examples in repo).
candidates.small_data_fit: Good for fine-tune track (designed for small datasets, strong augmentations), poor zero-shot for PC phase contrast.
candidates.notes: Keep as the classic baseline in the 5-fold CV comparison table; its matching module (IoU-based PQ/F1) is a convenient drop-in metric implementation. Does NOT give a neurite class. Instance masks: YES.

candidates.name: CellSAM (vanvalenlab, Caltech)
candidates.type: foundation model (SAM encoder + CellFinder box detector + box-prompted mask decoder)
candidates.what_it_does: Object detector (CellFinder) proposes boxes that prompt SAM to emit cell instance masks. Trained on 10 datasets (mammalian cells, yeast, bacteria; brightfield, fluorescence, phase included). Published in Nature Methods 2025 (s41592-025-02879-w); pip-installable; napari plugin; few-shot learning demonstrated (improves with a few annotated examples per domain).
candidates.pc12_fit: Phase contrast is in its training distribution, so zero-shot is plausible for cell bodies (medium estimate; paper claims human-level across modalities). The MIDL 2026 benchmark (checked) ranks CellSAM BELOW CellPose-SAM and μ-SAM+APG but above plain SAM/SAM3 on microscopy, with its weakest generalization under domain shift because each box maps 1:1 to a mask — a missed detection is unrecoverable. Neurites: NO — box-then-mask is a cell-body paradigm; a long neurite gets an ill-shaped box and a blobby mask.
candidates.neurite_support: No native neurite class; box prompt prior biased to compact objects
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (verified via GitHub API) for code; evaluation dataset includes Cellpose data under CC-BY-NC. SAM backbone itself: Apache-2.0 (facebookresearch/segment-anything, verified).
candidates.compute: Inference: SAM-ViT-L ~2.5 GB weights; comfortably on A5000 24 GB (few seconds/image with the detector+SAM cascade). Few-shot adaptation needs only a handful of annotated examples (paper demo) — no heavy training. Full fine-tuning of SAM components is NOT the intended workflow (repo ships inference + light adaptation only; no full training code).
candidates.small_data_fit: Good zero-shot/few-shot; not designed for full fine-tuning on your labels.
candidates.effort: Low (pip install git+...; one-line API segment_cellular_image)
candidates.notes: Worth running in the W6 zero-shot gate as the second zero-shot model (different failure mode from Cellpose: detector-driven). Instance masks: YES. No neurite class.

candidates.name: μ-SAM / micro-sam (computational-cell-analytics, Göttingen) — the 'SAM for microscopy' model family
candidates.type: foundation model (fully fine-tuned SAM + segmentation decoder + watershed/APG)
candidates.what_it_does: Fine-tunes the ENTIRE SAM for promptable microscopy segmentation, adds a decoder predicting foreground + boundary/center distances → watershed instance segmentation (AIS); MIDL 2026 adds automatic prompt generation (APG) on top, which 'consistently improves label-free microscopy and is competitive with CellPose-SAM' (their words; arXiv:2603.17845). Trained on ~17k light-microscopy images / >2M objects. Has pretrained light-microscopy models for cells, nuclei, bacteria, organoids, mitochondria.
candidates.pc12_fit: This is the most directly relevant model you named but misremembered as 'ISCE': the MIDL 2026 benchmark (checked in full) evaluates μ-SAM on exactly label-free (phase/differential-interference) microscopy cell datasets and μ-SAM+APG is a top-3 method on that modality. Zero-shot on PC12-style phase contrast: good-to-strong for cell bodies (evidence-backed). Neurites: NO native neurite model, but the architecture (distance-transform + watershed) and the repo's documented workflow explicitly support training new models from instance labelmaps — it is the most neurite-adjacent SAM tool. Even so, watershed-from-objects is still not built for 2-px thin tubes; you'd need neurite masks in training and should expect partial success, best verified empirically.
candidates.neurite_support: No pretrained neurite model; trainable on your neurite labelmaps (distance-transform+watershed is a reasonable but unproven prior for thin branching structures — treat as experiment, not plan)
candidates.license: MIT (verified via GitHub API) for micro-sam; SAM weights Apache-2.0
candidates.compute: Inference on A5000: fine (ViT-L). Training new model variants: repo ships training code (used to build the pretrained models) — on A6000 48 GB with n=70 images this is hours-to-one-overnight, not a problem.
candidates.small_data_fit: Zero-shot good (evidence); few-shot via promptable mode (click a cell) excellent for interactive validation; full fine-tune on n=70 plausible but the paper's models used 17k images — fine-tune from their pretrained checkpoint, don't train from scratch.
candidates.effort: Medium (pip install micro-sam; pretrained models auto-download; napari-based interactive workflow)
candidates.notes: Strong second recommendation alongside Cellpose-SAM; also the reference implementation of APG (free performance lift over AIS without retraining). Instance masks: YES. Cite μ-SAM + MIDL2026 benchmark paper for your architecture choices.

candidates.name: SAM / SAM 2 (facebookresearch, zero-shot with auto mask generation)
candidates.what_it_does: Prompt-based instance segmentation; 'zero-shot' = automatic mask generation (point grid + NMS) or manual/semi-auto point prompts.
candidates.pc12_fit: Weak-to-mediocre for automated batch cell segmentation in phase contrast. Evidence (MIDL 2026, checked): 'SAM itself fails at difficult microscopy segmentation tasks'; AMG 'performs worse for microscopy'; SAM2 was found inferior to SAM and 'did not segment any objects' on several datasets. For PC12 specifically (faint halo, low contrast, neurite clutter) zero-shot AMG will over- and under-segment badly. It shines as an INTERACTIVE tool: click-once/click-twice per cell gives near-human masks — useful for annotation workflow and XAI demos, not for the production gate. Fine-tuning SAM (LoRA/full) at 24-48 GB is feasible (LoRA fine-tunes in hours on a 24 GB card; full ViT-L fine-tune fits 48 GB), but you would be re-implementing what Cellpose-SAM/μ-SAM already did better for cells. SAM2 adds video — irrelevant for 2D stills.
candidates.compute: SAM-ViT-L inference ~2-4 GB VRAM; LoRA fine-tune 24 GB OK; full fine-tune 48 GB OK.
candidates.small_data_fit: Few-shot via prompting: yes. Full fine-tune at n=70: not worth it vs specialized models.
candidates.effort: Low for inference, High for meaningful adaptation
candidates.notes: Only worth including as (a) interactive annotation assistant, (b) negative-control baseline in the zero-shot gate to show why domain-specialized FMs matter. Instance masks: yes (per prompt). No neurite class.

candidates.name: HoVer-Net (Graham, Vu, ... Rajpoot; official PyTorch repo vqdang/hover_net)
candidates.type: trainable two-branch U-Net (horizontal+vertical instance + classification head)
candidates.what_it_does: U-Net with 2 heads: (1) horizontal & vertical distance-to-centroid channels → instance boundaries via local-maximum segmentation (separates touching/clustered objects), (2) type-prob head for per-instance classification. Pretrained CoNSeP/PanNuke/MoNuSAC/Kumar/CPM17 checkpoints (histology H&E). The instance head is the architectural ancestor of 'two-channel distance' instance networks used widely in nuclei work.
candidates.pc12_fit: Wrong-domain zero-shot (histology H&E only; no phase-contrast pretrained weights) — do NOT zero-shot it. Value is as the fine-tune architecture to study/compare: it is the closest architectural ancestor to a two-class (body+neurite) pipeline: you can (a) use the inst head to predict BODY instances, and (b) replace/augment the type head with a neurite-semantics head or run a second HoVer-Net instance head on a neurite channel. Small-data behavior: original trained on CoNSeP (~100 images) with strong augmentation — n≈70 is in the paper's regime, so 5-fold CV on your data is realistic; each fold's training is ~1 day on a 1080Ti per the paper's era → a few hours on A5000.
candidates.neurite_support: Not out of the box (heads are nucleus-instance + type). The H/V distance formulation works for any compact-ish object; for neurites you would need a dedicated branch or a different head — it is the right base to experiment on, not a neurite tool itself.
candidates.license: MIT (verified via GitHub API; note: PanNuke/MoNuSAC-derived checkpoints carry CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 per the README)
candidates.compute: Inference ~1-2 GB VRAM; training a 256x256-patch model: single A5000, hours per epoch, ~10-50 epochs → overnight per CV fold comfortably.
candidates.small_data_fit: Good (trained on ~100 images originally); augmentation pipeline (noise, shift, intensity) is part of the repo and important at n=70.
candidates.effort: Medium (patch extraction script, config.py-driven, some friction: torch 1.6 era code, Google-Drive checkpoints; PyTorch reimplementation reproduces paper results within 0.005 DICE)
candidates.notes: Use as your 'train-from-scratch' architecture candidate to compare against Cellpose-SAM fine-tuning; it directly yields per-instance outputs (bbox, centroid, contour, type) that feed your morphometrics and it is the honest baseline for the 'can a 2019 two-head U-Net beat a 2025 foundation model at n=70?' question — a strong thesis result either way. Instance masks: YES. No native neurite class.

candidates.name: SAM 3 (Meta, 2025)
candidates.what_it_does: Segment Anything v3: 'cell'-text-prompted direct instance segmentation, includes some microscopy in training.
candidates.pc12_fit: The MIDL 2026 benchmark (first systematic microscopy evaluation of SAM3, checked) shows SAM3 underperforms the microscopy-specialized FMs and is prompt-sensitive ('blob' sometimes beats 'cell'; 'nucleus' not recognized on some datasets). Zero-shot on PC12: medium-low estimate; useful as a novelty baseline, not as the workhorse.
candidates.code: https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3 (code status: check repo; paper arXiv:2506.18841)
candidates.compute: Large ViT; fine on A6000 48 GB; 24 GB tight but workable with fp16.
candidates.small_data_fit: Prompting only; no practical fine-tune path shipped.
candidates.notes: Mention in related work; optional baseline if time remains.

candidates.name: CellViT++ / CellViT (CellProfiler/2024-2025 foundation model for histopathology cells)
candidates.type: foundation model (ViT decoder over Cellpose/SAM encoders)
candidates.what_it_does: Foundation model for cell/nuclei segmentation benchmarked in kidney pathology studies (arXiv:2510.01287, 2411.00078 — both checked abstracts) against Cellpose/StarDist/Cellpose-SAM. Aimed at H&E tissue, not live-cell phase contrast.
candidates.pc12_fit: Domain mismatch (fixed histopathology). No PC12/phase-contrast evaluation found.
candidates.code: see CellProfiler ecosystem (not verified in depth)
candidates.notes: Histopathology-oriented; not worth the integration cost for a live-cell PC12 thesis. Included for completeness since it appears in 2025 benchmark papers.

candidates.name: MoCell
candidates.what_it_does: Unverified: no paper, arXiv record, or code repo under this name for cell segmentation could be located via arXiv full-text search, bioRxiv API, GitHub repo search, or Crossref. (GitHub 'MoCell' hits are unrelated: a 2019 MOEA evolutionary-algorithm paper and a 2025 terminal-tool.) Possibly a misremembered name (candidates: MoCell might be conflated with MoNuSeg, a 2018 nuclei SEGMENTATION DATASET, or with 'Micro-SAM').
candidates.notes: Do not cite. If the lab heard this name, ask for the paper link; otherwise drop from the survey.

candidates.name: DICE (foundation model, 2023-2025, per task brief)
candidates.type: claimed segmentation foundation model (from task brief)
candidates.what_it_does: Unverified as a 2023-2025 segmentation foundation model. The verified 'Dice' hits are: (a) DICE-XMBD (Front. Genet. 2021, github.com/xmuyulab/Dice-XMBD) — a 2021 U-Net-based IMC cell segmenter, NOT a foundation model; (b) the DICE loss function. No 2023-2025 'DICE' cell-segmentation foundation model with code was found via Crossref/GitHub/arXiv.
candidates.code: unverified (DICE-XMBD exists at github.com/xmuyulab/Dice-XMBD but is 2021 IMC-specific)
candidates.notes: Do not cite as a 2023-2025 foundation model. Possibly conflated with Dice loss or DICE-XMBD.

candidates.name: Cell-Clarity
candidates.what_it_does: Unverified as a cell-segmentation foundation model: no matching paper found on arXiv, bioRxiv API, Crossref, or GitHub. 'Cell-Clarity' appears in unrelated contexts (a single-cell transcriptomics evaluation context at Microsoft Research is about scRNA-seq FMs, not imaging). Possibly a misremembered name (candidates: CellCLIP? Cell-SAM? 'Cell-Classifier'?).
candidates.notes: Do not cite; request the original reference from whoever named it.

techniques.name: Human-in-the-loop fine-tuning (Cellpose 2.0 workflow) on n≈70 labeled images
techniques.how_it_helps: Turns 70 labeled PC12 images into a custom body-class model that should beat zero-shot; official, documented, GUI-supported; the BIBM2025 study (arXiv:2511.04803, abstract checked) empirically studies exactly this data-efficiency/transfer question for Cellpose.
techniques.verdict: adopt — this is the primary fine-tune track
techniques.effort: Low: hours of GPU + ~1-2 h of label QA per model
techniques.notes: Split by image (5 folds); use the second batch arriving in ~2 weeks as an independent external test to avoid overfit claims.

techniques.name: APG (automatic prompt generation) on μ-SAM — MIDL 2026
techniques.how_it_helps: Free performance lift on label-free microscopy with zero retraining; combines detector-derived point prompts with SAM promptable masks + NMS. Implemented and documented in micro-sam.
techniques.verdict: adopt — cheap win in W6 gate
techniques.notes: arXiv:2603.17845 (checked in full) — cite as the method for prompt-based instance refinement.

techniques.name: Prompt-engineered SAM via CellFinder-style detector (CellSAM strategy)
techniques.how_it_helps: Illustrates the three SAM→microscopy adaptation strategies (prompt-derived, decoder-on-encoder, full fine-tune) that the MIDL 2026 paper systematizes; useful framing for the thesis architecture chapter.
techniques.notes: Use the paper's taxonomy (strategies 1-3) to justify your architecture choice in the write-up.

techniques.name: Semi-supervised/unsupervised adaptation to unlabeled lab images (SelfAdapt, arXiv:2508.11411; fuzzy-logic + spatial stats GUI, arXiv:2508.15979)
techniques.how_it_helps: Your lab has unknown-count unlabeled phase-contrast images — SelfAdapt (ICCVW 2025, abstract checked) adapts Cellpose-style models to unlabeled target domains; a defensible W8-W10 experiment to harvest value from unlabeled data without labels.
techniques.verdict: watch — feasible stretch goal if W7 goes well
techniques.notes: Both papers benchmark against Cellpose/StarDist on phase-contrast, so their protocols transfer.

techniques.name: Two-head body+neurite network (HoVer-Net inst head + separate neurite head or dual-instance network)
techniques.how_it_helps: The only reviewed architecture that gives you BOTH a body instance output and a pluggable second semantic/instance head from a single backbone; closest architectural ancestor to your task (per task brief; verified against official repo README).
techniques.verdict: recommend as the in-house architecture candidate
techniques.effort: Medium (repo is 2019-era PyTorch; expect to modernize dataloader for 2-channel PC+fluo input)
techniques.notes: Train body head on body masks; for neurites, either (a) a second instance head trained on neurite masks, or (b) a segmentation head for the neurite class — the H/V distance trick does NOT generalize to thin tubes, so use plain binary segmentation for the neurite branch and let classical morphometrics (skeletonize → length/branch/angle) do the counting/length/angle extraction, matching the planned hybrid design.

techniques.name: Zero-shot gate protocol: 3 FMs × 2 modalities before any fine-tuning
techniques.how_it_helps: W6 gate: run cpsam_v2/cpdino (Cellpose), μ-SAM+APG (micro-sam), CellSAM, (+SAM-AMG as weak baseline) on all 70 labeled images; compute per-class DSC + clDice (neurite proxy = 'does anything capture the thin structures') + count error; the MIDL 2026 mSA/IoU-matching protocol (thresholds 0.5-0.95) is a ready-made metric recipe.
techniques.notes: Image-level 5-fold split from day 1; zero-shot numbers become the 'foundation model prior' row in every results table.

techniques.name: Neurite-specific representation: semantic mask + post-hoc graph (skeleton), not instance detection
techniques.how_it_helps: None of the verified FMs handles neurites as instances; the field's neurite tools (NeuroQuantify, AutoNeuriteJ — already in your known-prior-work list) treat neurites as a MASK and derive count/length/angle via skeletonization. Keep that split: FM/DL only proposes the binary neurite mask (fine-tune a U-Net branch or a second Cellpose-class model if you must), morphometrics (skimage.skeletonize → graph) does counting/length/direction. This keeps every metric (clDice, Betti error) well-defined.
techniques.notes: Betti-0/Betti-1 of the neurite mask graph gives exactly the topology error you planned to report.

bold_ideas.idea: Neurite-aware two-class flow-field (Cellpose-style vectors) with a tubular shape prior: train the flow decoder on BOTH body and neurite labelmaps from your 70+ images, adding a small anisotropy-aware loss so thin tubes get directed flow instead of star-convex collapse.
bold_ideas.why_now: Cellpose-SAM proves the flow-decoder+foundation-backbone recipe generalizes superhumanly (bioRxiv 2025.04.28.651001, checked); nobody has published a flow-field model for PC12 neurite classes — the gap is real and the code (cellpose train pipeline) is MIT/BSD-licensed and 2-student-sized.
bold_ideas.feasibility: High: reuse Cellpose training code, swap in 2-class labels; 70 images is enough because you fine-tune from their pretrained weights; 5-fold CV overnight on A5000.
bold_ideas.risk: Star-convex dynamics may still truncate 2-px branches; mitigation = keep the neurite branch as plain semantic segmentation and only apply the flow field to bodies (i.e., the safe version is exactly the two-head HoVer-Net-style plan).
bold_ideas.differentiator: First flow-field body+neurite joint model on phase contrast for a small-data thesis; directly feeds clDice + Betti metrics.
bold_ideas.verdict: feasible and differentiated — make it the 'novelty' claim with the two-head U-Net as the safe fallback.

bold_ideas.idea: APG-style prompt recycling: use zero-shot Cellpose-SAM/μ-SAM predictions as pseudo-labels to pretrain the in-house two-head network, then fine-tune on the 70 human labels (semi-supervised distillation; pattern proven in kidney-pathology studies arXiv:2411.00078 / 2510.01287, abstracts checked).
bold_ideas.why_now: You have unknown-quantity unlabeled lab images + 70 labeled ones; distillation is the standard, publishable bridge between foundation-model priors and small labeled data.
bold_ideas.feasibility: High: inference + label export from both FMs is trivial; train with the HoVer-Net or nnU-Net codebase.
bold_ideas.risk: Pseudo-label error in thin neurites could teach wrong topology; gate with clDice before/after pseudo-training.
bold_ideas.differentiator: Quantifies 'how much of the gain is the foundation model prior' — a clean ablation the reviewers will like.

bold_ideas.idea: Betti-guided loss: add Betti-0/Betti-1 (Euler characteristic / persistent homology on the neurite mask) of the predicted mask to the segmentation loss so the network is explicitly penalized for broken/extra branches.
bold_ideas.why_now: You already plan Betti error as a report metric; making it a training signal is a genuine, small, verifiable contribution (topological losses exist in the MRI/vascular literature but not for neurite morphometrics at this scale).
bold_ideas.feasibility: High: Betti numbers of a binary 2D mask are cheap (scikit-image + giotto-tda or pure connected-component counting); loss term = |B1_pred - B1_gt| per image.
bold_ideas.risk: Gradient flow through topology is non-smooth; use the relaxed Euler-characteristic (boundary pixel count + component count) formulation instead of exact persistence.
bold_ideas.differentiator: Ties the XAI/topology story (your Betti metric) to the model itself — a coherent thesis narrative.
bold_ideas.verdict: feasible stretch goal for W10+; cheap to try, easy to drop.

bottom_line: For the W6 zero-shot gate, run three verified, runnable foundation models on all 70 labeled images and keep the MIDL 2026 (arXiv:2603.17845) head-to-head as your justification: (1) Cellpose-SAM (cpsam_v2 or cpdino) — BSD-3 code, CC-BY-NC weights (fine for a thesis), best-documented fine-tuning on exactly your data scale, and the only FM ecosystem with a working human-in-the-loop training loop; (2) μ-SAM via micro-sam with APG (MIT) — top-3 on label-free microscopy in the benchmark and trainable on your own labelmaps; (3) CellSAM (Apache-2.0) as an independent detector-driven baseline. Expect all three to produce good cell-body instance masks on phase contrast (instance counting is solved by any of them) and none to produce neurite structures — every verified FM in this space is star-convex/box/compact-object centric, so neurites MUST stay a separate semantic-mask branch with classical skeleton-based morphometrics (count/length/angle from skimage graph; clDice + Betti on that mask). Fine-tune track: fine-tune Cellpose-SAM (a few hours on the A5000, image-level 5-fold) as the primary, keep HoVer-Net (MIT, small-data-proven, the two-head ancestor) as the honest in-house architecture baseline, and use the unlabeled lab images via pseudo-label distillation or SelfAdapt as the stretch result. Drop MoCell, 'DICE' and Cell-Clarity from the survey: no primary source exists under those names (verified negative), and treat 'ISCE' as a misremembering of μ-SAM/micro-sam. License posture for your deliverable is clean: BSD-3 (Cellpose, StarDist), MIT (micro-sam, HoVer-Net code; PanNuke-derived checkpoints CC-BY-NC-SA — avoid those checkpoints), Apache-2.0 (CellSAM, SAM) — all fine for a free, non-commercial student tool, with the only NC caveat being Cellpose's pretrained weights and dataset.
